data.theorem_title: Zipf–Mandelbrot law with Hurwitz-zeta normalization is a distribution
data.formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem zipfMandelbrotPMF_hasSum_one (q s : ℝ) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hs : 1 < s) :
    HasSum (fun k : ℕ => zipfMandelbrotPMF q s k) 1 := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
data.natural_language_statement:
Let $s>1$ and $q\ge0$. With normalizing constant $C=\zeta(s,q+1)=\sum_{k\ge1}(k+q)^{-s}$ (Hurwitz zeta), the Zipf–Mandelbrot frequencies
$$f(k;q,s)=\frac{1}{C}\,\frac{1}{(k+q)^s},\qquad k=1,2,3,\dots$$
form a probability distribution:
$$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}f(k;q,s)=1 .$$
data.source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law), snapshot uploaded by the proposer, section "Related laws" ($f(k;N,q,s)=\frac1C\frac1{(k+q)^s}$; "The constant C is the Hurwitz zeta function evaluated at s").

For all reals $q\ge0$ and $s>1$: the family $k\mapsto\mathrm{zipfMandelbrotPMF}(q,s,k)$, $k\in\mathbb N$ (value $0$ at $k=0$, and $1/\big(\zeta_{\mathrm{ser}}(s,q+1)(k+q)^s\big)$ for $k\ge1$, where $\zeta_{\mathrm{ser}}(s,a)=\sum_{n\ge0}(n+a)^{-s}$ as a `tsum`), is summable with sum exactly $1$ (Lean `HasSum`, i.e. unconditional convergence).
